rationale: Base rate 0.05 (Democrats won 0 of about 12 Texas Senate races since 1990; about 10 of 11 in Michigan). Strong evidence moves it up: Talarico leads Paxton by 2-4 points in October polls (Emerson, Marist, UT, TPOR), and El-Sayed is the nominee, up about 2 points on Rogers (Lean D). Texas polls have historically overstated Democrats, so Talarico is about 45%; with correlated outcomes, the joint chance is about a third. A Michigan search result quoted prediction-market odds; I discarded it.

Base rate 0.88 (Democrats won 9 of 10 Minnesota Senate races since 2000). Flanagan leads Tafoya by about 3-5 points in averages (RCP +3.4, others +4.6/+5.2). Tafoya's fraud-scandal message and the open seat add some risk, so I set it slightly below the base. A result quoted a Polymarket price; I discarded it.

Base rate 0.10 (share of ECB meetings with a hike since 1999). Previews (FXStreet, Reuters poll) expect a hold at 2.50% on Oct 29, with the next hike in December despite inflation near 3.7-3.8%. Strong consensus for a hold three days before the meeting. One result cited OIS-implied odds; I flagged it and did not use the number.

Base rate 0.75 that a fragile ceasefire survives about 3 more weeks (few cases). Netanyahu reportedly ordered preparations for new strikes, and the US and Israel are threatening renewed strikes. Trump reportedly opposes restarting the war before the Nov 3 midterms, which leaves a Nov 4-15 window. Diplomacy is stalled and the Lebanon dispute is unresolved, so I set it below the base rate.

Base rate 0.97 (Republicans won every South Carolina Senate race since 2000). Polls are unusually close, with the Republican nominee up only about 2 points; Andrews has raised far more, and some sources conflict on who the nominee is. South Carolina polls have historically understated Republicans (Graham-Harrison 2020), so the Republican side remains a clear favorite but well below the base.

Base rate 0.15 (Democrats won 1 of the last 7 Ohio governor races). Strong evidence moves it up: Acton leads Ramaswamy by about 3 points in averages (270toWin 49.0-45.8; Marist +7, Fox +2), and Sabato moved the race to Lean D on Oct 22. Ohio's recent tendency for polls to understate Republicans tempers this. One result quoted a Kalshi price; I discarded it.

Base rate 0.70 (a majority party on 53 seats usually holds the Senate in a midterm). Strong evidence moves it down: non-market models give Democrats 56-85% (Silver 75%, DDHQ 56%, Poliwave 57%), and Democrats lead in Texas, Ohio, Alaska and others. Republicans have about a 30% chance. One aggregator result cited Polymarket and Kalshi figures; I discarded them.

Base rate 0.02 that a general ceasefire is agreed in any given week of a long war. The only new agreement is a local humanitarian truce in Oleshky, which does not qualify. The next trilateral talks are planned for mid-November, and the Kremlin rejects a general pause. Five days remain.

Base rate 0.88 (incumbent senators win most general elections). Strong evidence moves it down: Peltola is running and leads Sullivan by about 1-2 points in averages (DDHQ 49.0-46.6, RCP +0.8), with ranked-choice voting in play. Alaska polls have understated Republicans before (2020 Sullivan won by 12), so Sullivan is a slight underdog. One result quoted market odds; I discarded them.

Base rate 0.10 for a named model release in a specific 5-day window. As of Oct 23-25, Anthropic's pages still list Fable 5.1 as the newest Fable model. Leaks (an Azure catalog ID, a TestingCatalog report that it reached partners and could come 'next week') make a release soon plausible, but the earlier claimed dates passed without a release. The Oct 26 IPO S-1 filing may also slow announcements.

This is the probability of the 'No Hormuz Agreement' outcome. Base 0.90, since a specific US-Iran deal within about a week is rare. Talks have been stalled for weeks; Iran insists on its conditions (lift the blockade first), and Qatari mediators are stuck on sequencing. With US-Israeli strike threats active and only 7 days left, a jointly announced agreement looks unlikely.

Base rate 0.03 for a ceasefire agreement within 5 days during active fighting. There is an unconfirmed Israel Hayom report of a Saudi offer of $1B through Iran and a Saudi visit to Tehran. Riyadh reportedly rejects a new ceasefire until territory is returned, and Houthi strikes on Saudi airports continued as of Oct 25. I set it slightly above the base for the back-channel.
